subject: AcmeMed: questions on log retention, deletion, and exception process
body:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acmemed.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.example.com
Cc: privacy@acmemed.com, sarah.li@acmemed.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on log retention / CAIQ items

Hi Laura / Rafael,

We're working through the SIG and CAIQ for our procurement team and there are a couple of items we need clarified around data and log retention before we can proceed to legal review:

- Required retention: AcmeMed's policy requires audit/access logs to be retained for up to 36 months for compliance. Can Redwood confirm the maximum retention windows for: application request logs, auth/access logs, admin audit trails, and system metrics?
- Deletion requests: What is the SLA/process when a customer asks for complete deletion of their account and related logs? How do you handle backups and cached KV entries (TTL)?
- Customer-specific exceptions: If negotiation leads to a longer retention term (e.g., 3 years) are there templates for exception approval and what controls are required?
- Evidence: For our audit, we need SOC 2 evidence that retention/deletion is enforced and a CAIQ answer pointing to the controls.

We'd appreciate a short table and any evidence artifacts. I've attached the CAIQ snippets where AcmeMed flagged the items.

Thanks,
John
John Doe
Director, InfoSec
AcmeMed Health

John — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rafa (sales) and Mina (security/compliance) and Evelyn (legal) to capture the operational, contractual and legal pieces.

Quick answers high-level, details below and attached:
- Default retention: application request logs (365 days), auth/access logs (365 days), admin audit trails (365 days), system metrics (90 days).
- KV cache: ephemeral by design; default TTL is 7 days and we don't persist KV cache beyond that unless explicitly configured.
- Deletion requests: standard account deletion removes primary customer data and starts a propagation to caches/backups; typical propagation/complete removal target is 30 days, with backups scrubbed on the next backup cycle.
- Exceptions: we can grant contractual exceptions to extend retention up to 36 months for audit logs; this requires DPA/SOW amendment and an exception approval form.

Attached: logs-retention-matrix.csv (mapping by log type), SOC2-Data-Retention-Controls.pdf (excerpt of relevant controls).

Next steps: Rafa — can you propose the exception template and commercial terms? Mina/Evelyn — please confirm the technical and legal evidence and any additional controls required for HIPAA/EU residency.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all — inserting some technical specificity so you have what procurement and infosec need for the SIG/CAIQ mapping.

Retention windows (defaults):
- Request / inference logs: persisted for 365 days. These include request metadata (timestamp, model variant, token usage, request id). Request payloads are not retained beyond the retention period unless customer opt-in is configured.
- Auth / access logs: 365 days. Includes admin console access, API key rotations, and IAM events.
- Admin audit trails: 365 days. Covers configuration changes and role assignments.
- System metrics & host logs: 90 days (rolled and aggregated).
- KV cache: TTL 7 days by default and not backed up. If a customer opts to persist longer, that is a customer-managed config and treated as stored customer data.

Deletion process:
- Customer-initiated deletion triggers a workflow: 1) mark account and associated data for deletion; 2) remove live data and purge caches; 3) schedule backups containing that data for secure overwrite on the next backup retention cycle (typically within 30 days). We maintain an audit trail of deletion requests and completions.
- Backups: immutable backups are rotated; we perform cryptographic erasure when allowed by the backup provider and schedule. For contracts requiring hard-delete attestations, we include a remediation timeline and certificate of deletion.

Exceptions and controls:
- We will allow contractual extension to 36 months for audit logs with a signed exception form, SOW, and agreed compensating controls (encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, dedicated tenant isolation or Dedicated capacity, and enhanced monitoring).
- For EU residency/HIPAA workloads: recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated in an EU region. That also allows contractually enforced data residency and stricter retention controls.

Evidence we can provide: SOC 2 report excerpts that map to retention controls (attached), CAIQ answers (linkable), and audit logs demonstrating deletion workflows. For SIG, we can populate the relevant sections and provide exported CSVs on request.

Mina Haddad

John — attaching the signed DPA and including language for backup scrub attestations. High level:
- Backup deletion/scrub attestation: Redwood will confirm via certificate of deletion that backups which contained deleted customer data will be securely overwritten/scrubbed within 30 days of the deletion workflow completion. The certificate includes timestamps and the backup identifiers involved.
- EU residency: we can provision Redwood Private in the EU (or Dedicated capacity in an EU region) — timeline typically 6–8 weeks from SOW signature for Private (shorter for Dedicated depending on capacity). When provisioned as EU-only, logs and backups are configured to remain in-region; contractual language will reflect that restriction.
- Exception workflow: to extend retention to 36 months we require: signed exception form, SOW amendment, acceptance of compensating controls (customer-managed KMS or Redwood-hosted CMEK), and an agreed SLA/financial addendum.

I've uploaded the signed DPA to DocuSign here: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/SAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID and attached the signed PDF for your record. Rafael — please coordinate the exception template + pricing and we'll turn that into a formal SOW when AcmeMed approves.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
